sections.title: Canvas setup and cell list start
sections.what: Sets up the full-window canvas, scales it to the device, and begins the list of cells sized from the window width.
sections.why: Scaling to the device keeps the drawing sharp.
sections.watch_out: The size is read once at the start.

sections.name: PixelTransition: for
sections.title: Creating the cells
sections.what: Splits the window into random rectangles, gives each a start time based on distance from the centre, and marks some as falling fragments.
sections.why: Outer pieces start first, so the break seems to spread from the middle.
sections.watch_out: Random values mean each run differs slightly.

sections.name: PixelTransition (part 3)
sections.title: Animating the break and the fall
sections.what: Each frame, shrinks cells in the break phase, fills a dark backdrop during the fall, moves fragments into depth, and calls the done callback at the end.
sections.why: Hands control back to the page once the effect has finished.
sections.watch_out: The done callback is stored in a reference so a changed callback does not restart the animation.

summary: A short full-screen animation in which the page breaks into dark squares that fall into depth, then calls a done function.
purpose: Plays as a transition into the Atlas page.
why: Gives the move to the Atlas a visual break. The done callback is what starts the navigation.
how: Splits the window into random rectangles that start to shrink at times based on distance from the centre. Some become falling fragments. After the break, the fragments move into depth, then the done callback runs.
inputs: An active flag and a done callback.
outputs: A full-window canvas during the animation, then nothing. Calls the done callback once at the end.
risks: The canvas size is set from the window size at the start, so resizing during the animation is not handled. Random layout means each run looks different.
debug: If navigation never happens, check that the done callback is called at the end of the frame loop. If the screen is blurry, check the device pixel ratio setting. If the effect stays on screen, check the active flag and the cleanup.
